This article is absolutely dripping with bias and looks like something that would come off a Tumblr blog. Weirdly, clicking their name to try and find more pieces gets you a 403 and they show up absolutely nowhere in Google.

I agree with some of the points made, but some of them are a bit of a stretch.

For example:

>Science Thinks Humans are Special

How does that define science as a religion? There are plenty of religions that operate on the principles that humans are actually much more inferior than we believe. Buddhism, for example, involves learning a lot of humility and a removal of one's ego. This is a pretty weak point to try and connect the two.

>It Casts Out Heretics and Persecutes all Other Religions

A stretch. Scientists have long been literally persecuted by religious people, whereas even in modern times the only "persecution" science is guilty of are fighting against those who are trying to force their religious views on others around them.

>Science Reveres Its Own Saints

There's a difference between recognizing someone's achievements and literally worshiping someone. As for Galileo, he was never supposed to be credited with discovering heliocentricity, and any educated person knows that. He was a defender of the idea because of the observations made with the advances he made in telescopes. He would defend this position against the Catholic church even though it would result in him being imprisoned and then later on house arrest for the rest of his life.

>Science Makes up Stories to Explain Our Origins

Comparing campfire legends to a scientific model based on observable facts is absolutely ridiculous.

Also, this entire paragraph:

>You know what its latest version of this story is? In the beginning, there were giant membranes. These membranes touched each other, triggering something called the “Big Bang”. Sure.

>Science is Based on Established Dogmas

The difference between science and religion is science is willing to change based on new evidence. You don't see people bloodletting any more do you? Because we figured out it didn't work, and we stopped doing it. No matter how "devoted" someone was to the idea, it died as a practice because we learned from out mistakes. On the other side of that coin, some of the biggest religions in the world still practice thousand year old rituals and moral decisions even though the general population and even those of their own sect have long dismissed the ideas.

>Science Will Bend to Accommodate Modern Trends

Breaking news: Scientists still humans open to things like bias, misunderstanding, and greed. Once again, the difference is, when these lies are exposed, they are quickly shunned and dismissed by the scientific community in favor of new and better evidence, which the author even admits to:

>Instead I will use the scientific approach to homosexuality. It was included in the list of personality disorders of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorder (DSM) up to its 1973 edition. It was then removed – only to be replaced a year later by a close variant, before being removed entirely in 1986

>Most of Science is Unfounded

Absolutely hogwash. They didn't even make a point here they basically just said "PROVE TO ME THAT DARK MATTER EXISTS"

>Science Requires Faith

You're right, because science is about asking questions and sometimes you don't know the answer beforehand. The difference between science and a religion is that the faith in the answers comes from past experience and past evidence and that faith is only as strong as the new evidence. You'll be hard pressed to find a respected scientists who will cling to a theory for dear life after being proven wrong even if his theory was only based on a gut instinct.

This whole list was awful. I mean yeah, if you want to be pedantic about it, any system of beliefs, even those based on facts over faith could be described as a religion.

I agree with others that this article is written with a heavy amount of bias, though I do believe there are some valid points in here to a degree. I think many here would acknowledge the fanaticism with which reddit users for instance exhibit toward richard dawkins, Niel degrass tyson, bill nye, etc. And how many of us have observed people getting excited over this or that project because "SCIENCE!" even when it has nothing to do with science. This is the layman reactionary culture that idolizes science, scientists, and celebrities, and which mocks openly anyone who does not toe the line. Conspiracy theorists, homeopath users, those opposed to vaccinations, global warming critics, etc. - these people are not human - they are vile scum worthy of every scoff and joke and derogatory term imaginable to the science obsessed culture.

Of course that isn't actual science.

Actual science is peer review journals, government funding, research and experimentation and nobel prizes. If your work isn't in a peer reviewed journal, well then your work means nothing. And if your area of interest is in something taboo, then you aren't going to be getting into any journals anytime soon - especially not with your reputation as a sensible professional intact. Here's a brief article illustrating this challenge the scientific establishment must overcome: http://amasci.com/tesla/ballsci.html

Well actually that isn't science either. That's the scientific establishment we have created as a society. It works great most of the time.

I think it should be obvious to any student of anthropology that humans have a tendency to adopt habits that resemble religious fervor. The tribalism, the magical thinking, idolatry, etc. And it should be obvious to any student of anthropology that humans also all suffer the same failings of greed, fear of rejection, pride, and often a mistrust of anything new or different which can degrade into intense emotion, as well as being susceptible to political manipulations. I don't believe science as a philosophy or a process is a religion, and i do think that the people who work in the culture of the scientific establishment, and those who obsess over it, sometimes do suffer these very normal human failings - just the same as religious adherents and proselytizers do.

just my two cents.

edit: and just to be clear, the culture that idolizes science is not a bad thing in itself. Much better to value scientific development than to obsess over war and destruction or on blatant superstition, or dancing with the stars or honey-boo-boo.

    The article claims that science is another religion. To justify it lists 10 reasons. A manoeuvre pretending to be logical deduction.

  • What is the article missing?

    The concept of what is religion and what is science. One can't logically establish that object A belongs to category A without linking essential characteristics of A with observed characteristics of A.

    Not waste much time over the article. It is a hit job, and should be taken like one. If one has to necessarily respond, how about the following proposition:

Proposition: Science advances by seeking consistency with reality. Religion advances by seeking consistency with its own stories, even at the cost of consistency with reality.
